question.problem: Which of the following gives the arc length of the polar curve $r=1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{4}?$
question.worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\sqrt{(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}+(-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\sqrt{(1-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )+{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\sqrt{1-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +1}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\sqrt{2-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta \,.\end{aligned}
$$
